---
title: "Notation and conventions"
---

## Units and state {#sec-unit-table}

| Symbol / quantity | Convention |
|---|---|
| `a`, `z` | Scale factor and redshift, `a=1/(1+z)` |
| `tau` | Dimensionless supercomoving expansion clock, @eq-clock |
| `rho`, `p`, `E`, `v`, `B` | MHD code quantities, not unqualified cgs values |
| `psi` | Mixed-GLM divergence-cleaning scalar |
| `gamma` | Gas adiabatic index |
| `rho_b(z)` | Physical mean baryon density used for cgs conversion |
| `B0_ng` | Comoving magnetic amplitude in nG at the declared normalization epoch/band |
| `B_phys` | Physical field in G, @eq-field-units |
| `v_unit` | `MHD_CHEM_VUNIT`, cm/s |
| `T` | Gas temperature, K; `T_CMB=2.725(1+z) K` |
| `x_HII` | Hydrogen ionization fraction; not the total electron fraction |
| `xe_total` | Electrons per hydrogen nucleus including the selected helium model |
| `HII`, `H2I`, `HeII` arrays | Stored species payloads; interpret mass weighting and centered/neutral storage before reading as fractions |
| `R` | `3*rho_b*c^2/(4*rho_gamma_energy)` in the photon model |
| `lambda_gamma` | Physical Thomson mean free path; divided by physical box in code closure |
| `q` | `k_phys*lambda_gamma`, dimensionless |

Coordinates are periodic in a unit code cube for the production runner.
Cell centers are `(i-1/2)/N`; Fourier integer modes use `2*pi*n/L`, with the
forward transform convention `exp(-i*k*x)` and inverse `exp(+i*k*x)`. RFFT
storage keeps the first spatial axis as a half spectrum. A fourth transform
dimension in the photon workspace is a channel, not a spatial coordinate.

## Wavenumbers and spectra {#sec-wavenumbers}

The physical TOML box is `L_h=cosmology.box_ckpc_h`, a comoving length in ckpc/h.
Its length in ckpc is `L_h/h`. Magnetic `kcut`, `kmax`, and the spectrum's
numeric `k` follow the driver's coordinate box `L_s=MHD_BOXSIZE` (default 1),
not an implicit unit inferred from a TSV filename. To convert coordinate
length to comoving Mpc without h:

$$
u_L=\frac{10^{-3}L_h}{hL_s}\ {\rm cMpc},\qquad
k_{\rm cMpc^{-1}}=k_{\rm input}/u_L,\qquad
P_{\rm cMpc^3}=P_{\rm input}u_L^3.
$$ {#eq-spectrum-units}

Field-amplitude factors remain: magnetic/force/velocity spectra retain code
amplitudes unless separately converted. For dimensionless density contrast,
power has only coordinate-volume units.

The estimator uses normalized Fourier amplitudes and `P=V*mean(|fhat|^2)`
over occupied modes, summing vector components where applicable. The radial
`k` value is the occupied-mode mean, not necessarily the geometric bin center.
`mu=abs(k_axis)/|k|`; isotropic reductions weight each angular bin by `Nmodes`.

$$
\Delta^2(k)=\frac{k^3P(k)}{2\pi^2}.
$$ {#eq-dimensionless-power}

This combination is invariant under the coordinate-length conversion above.
Keep empty bins as missing. State windowing, finite-volume/CIC effects, physical
band limits, shell averaging, and any additional smoothing when comparing power.

## Normalization and diagnostics {#sec-estimators}

`Brms=sqrt(mean(Bx^2+By^2+Bz^2))`. Reference-band normalization and total-band
normalization are different as described in [initial conditions](initial-conditions.qmd).
`divBdx_over_brms` uses the centered-grid divergence and grid spacing divided
by measured magnetic RMS. It is a numerical diagnostic, not a proof of exact
continuum solenoidality.

`delta_b_rms` and `delta_dm_rms` measure density contrasts; they are not raw
density standard deviations in g/cm3. Density PDFs are volume-weighted per
`log10(rho/reference density)`. Pressure/tension power requires a cross term,
@eq-cross-spectrum. The photon energy ledger tracks resolved perturbation
energy; algebraically eliminated higher-multipole heat is outside that ledger.

## Phase comparisons {#sec-phase-convention}

Keep signed complex amplitudes when comparing linear references. Sine and
cosine ICs differ by phase; taking absolute values can hide a sign/clock error.
A magnetic sine forcing produces quadratic `2k` terms; compare the observable's
mode, not automatically the magnetic fundamental. Match cell centers,
polarization, guide-field orientation, exact output epochs, and peculiar-velocity
units before forming a relative error.
